operator_io_quirks: All 15 tables report rows=0: original is empty; original_values/original_sizes are all empty/0, so TS samplers get no original elements and p=1 fresh draws dominate.
publication.cid is declared TEXT but is an FK to conference.cid (INT): declared-type dispatch gives String fuzzer, yet FK fill copies integer parent values -> storage class contradicts declared type.
publication.year is declared INT and named 'year': extract_typed_values rewrites whole-word 'year' to 'yearplaceholderrare' before parsing; column lookup must strip that suffix.
cite has NO primary key (pk=[]): sample_fresh_primary_keys must be a no-op there; drop_unique_duplicates also no-op (no unique cols).
cite has two FKs to the SAME parent publication.pid (cited, citing): self-ish many-to-one, both draw from publication's final pid list.

Composite PKs everywhere in the junction tables (domain_author, domain_conference, domain_journal, domain_keyword, domain_publication, publication_keyword, writes): composite-PK members get max_l0=30, not inf.
Junction tables have two FK columns and no other columns: every column is FK-filled, so their row content is entirely parent-value copies; PK dedup then drops many rows.
DDL uses backtick-quoted parent refs (`author`("aid")) in domain_author/domain_conference: pragma foreign_key_list still resolves; parent_exists=true for all.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE constraints anywhere: TS never sets p=0 for checked, and insert failures are only PK/type-affinity related.
Table order: domain is a hub (7 children); publication depends on conference+journal; junction tables sit at the deepest level -> level-size growth x4 capped at 2500 makes junctions large.
journal column order is homepage,jid,name (jid not first): column_order must follow pragma order, not PK order.
No mixed-case or spaced identifiers; all lowercase, no views/triggers/indexes in DDL.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer (scale=0, is_int) for all INT columns: uniform ints in [-1,1] then +-1/+-2 perturbation -> tiny integer domain, heavy PK collisions before dedup.
String fuzzer (length 20) for homepage/name/abstract/title/keyword/continent: random a-zA-Z 0-9() strings with 50% contaminate -> implausible names, no real keywords.
publication.cid via String fuzzer produces text like 'aB3()' while FK fill (if cid treated as FK) copies conference.cid ints: mixed storage in one column.
Empty original => elements list is only the literal pool; with no train SQL pool, every column is pure fresh random -> FN from implausible values (e.g. year not in 1900-2020, names not real).
FK fill draws with replacement from parent's final values: junction tables get many duplicate (did,aid) pairs, then PK dedup keeps first -> small junction tables, FP risk from missing ties.
cite has no PK: no dedup, so duplicate (cited,citing) rows survive -> self-citation and duplicate edges appear; queries counting citations may over/under-count vs real.
publication.year INT fuzzer yields values in {-2..2} typically: year filters (year>2000) return empty -> FN on year predicates.
Level-size branch (0.5 prob) makes junction tables up to 2500 rows while parents may be ~30: FK fill with replacement from 30 parents gives massive duplication.
Number list_max quirk: with no elements, full range [-1,1] used; with pool elements, upper end overwritten to full max -> pool values only anchor the lower end.
String contaminate drops/prefixes chars: LIKE '%x%' predicates rarely match real-looking substrings -> FN on LIKE.
Composite PK dedup on junction tables after FK fill: rows_failed small, but effective row count << requested size -> cardinality-sensitive queries (COUNT) diverge.
No unique single-column constraints: drop_unique_duplicates never fires; only PK dedup shapes tables.
